payload.claim: This re-derives the sha256 of `raw` by calling `hashlib.sha256(raw.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()` instead of importing and calling `saffron.agents.artifacts.hash_artifact`, which is the exact helper `saffron/cell/session.py:3380` uses to produce `reviewed_diff_sha256` in the first place. The two computations agree today, but per the one-source rule a restated helper is a finding even when its value agrees with the original: if `hash_artifact` is ever changed (e.g. a different encoding or normalization), this inline copy in `qualify.py` silently stops matching and no gate (format/lint/types/tests) would notice, since both are just string-literal computations that happen to coincide.
